Let's go abroad.

Ukraine took another heavy beating — Russian strikes killed at least six people on Friday across the Dnipropetrovsk region and Kharkiv, some by cluster munitions, and Moscow threw a hundred and forty-seven drones at the country overnight, of which air defences knocked down a hundred and fourteen.

Kyiv's hitting back at Russian logistics hubs, but the tempo on both sides just keeps climbing.

Bigger picture from the health desk: the American regulator approved the country's first-ever mRNA flu vaccine, Moderna's shot for adults fifty and up.

It's the same platform as the Covid jabs, ran about twenty-seven percent more effective than a standard flu shot in a forty-thousand-person trial, and should be out for this winter's season.

A milestone, whatever your feelings on the tech.

And one for you specifically.

A Texas team built a little ultrasound patch you wear on your head that nudges deep brain regions during sleep.

In a small twenty-eight-person trial in Nature Communications, it got people into REM sleep about forty-three minutes faster and kept them there longer — no drugs, no surgery.

Early days and a tiny sample, but if it scales, that's real recovery tech for anyone training hard.

— personal items —

And your word of the day: drop knee.

It's that move where you turn a knee inward and down over a foothold to twist your hip into the wall — the Egyptian, some call it — so you can reach further with less pull on your arms.

As in, "I dropped a knee and suddenly the next hold was right there."

One quick productivity trick to go with it: the two-minute rule — if something lands on your plate that'd take under two minutes, just do it on the spot instead of filing it away.

The small stuff never piles up that way.
